title: Separate tiled dataflow from schedule choices

source.title: TileLang: A Composable Tiled Programming Model for AI Systems
source.claim_scope: A tiled programming abstraction evaluated across AI kernels; individual schedules still require target-specific validation.

implementation_recipe: Write one canonical tile-level dataflow before choosing thread binding, layout, tensorization, or pipeline depth.
Generate candidates by changing one schedule axis and at least one joint schedule combination.
Keep shape guards and tail handling explicit so specialization does not silently narrow correctness.
validation_recipe: Use the same dataflow and correctness oracle across schedule candidates.
Screen anchor and edge shapes before expanding the schedule neighborhood.
Record compiled resource usage so a faster tile is not mistaken for a universally better schedule.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Larger tiles reduce redundant movement but may increase registers, shared memory, and tail waste.
Layout changes can move cost between global coalescing, shared-memory conflicts, and compute utilization.
failure_modes: The search changes only scalar tile sizes and never explores a materially different ownership model.
A schedule wins the anchor shape but regresses weighted edge cases.
Compiler lowering does not preserve the intended tensorization or pipeline.
scope_limits: A programming model's reported SOTA results are not a performance guarantee for a new operator.
Schedule separation does not replace a global opportunity model.

candidate_archetypes.name: dataflow-fixed layout alternatives
candidate_archetypes.template: Hold tile dataflow fixed and implement coalesced, conflict-avoiding, and compute-native layouts as separate candidates.

candidate_archetypes.name: resource-bounded tile frontier
candidate_archetypes.template: Choose a few tile points that represent different register/shared-memory/parallelism regimes instead of a dense sweep.
